title: vehicle_params
description: Single source of physical truth for the vehicle (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md). Every leaf field carries a machine-readable 'units' annotation and, where a sign convention applies, a 'sign_convention' annotation. Consumers (tools/gen_params.py and everything downstream) must validate against this schema and refuse to start on a mismatch (rule 06-2).

pacejka_params.description: Magic Formula tire model coefficients. Null until a Phase 3 sysid fit exists (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md, claude-docs/07-sim-and-sysid.md).

pwm_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
pwm_us.description: Raw servo PWM pulse width for this calibration point.

angle_rad.description: Measured road-wheel angle produced by pwm_us.

mount_x_m.sign_convention: REP-103 base_link frame: x forward positive
mount_x_m.description: Sensor mounting offset from base_link origin along x. Null until Phase 2 ingest-board measurement (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md, roadmap 2.1/2.2).

mount_y_m.sign_convention: REP-103 base_link frame: y left positive
mount_y_m.description: Sensor mounting offset from base_link origin along y. Null until Phase 2 measurement.

mount_z_m.sign_convention: REP-103 base_link frame: z up positive
mount_z_m.description: Sensor mounting offset from base_link origin along z. Null until Phase 2 measurement.

mount_yaw_rad.description: Sensor mounting yaw relative to base_link. Null until Phase 2 measurement.

timestamp_offset_s.description: Fixed timestamp offset from the ingest board's shared clock, per the sync design doc (roadmap 2.2). Null until that doc exists.

mass_kg.description: Total vehicle mass, including onboard compute.

wheelbase_m.description: Distance between front and rear axles (cg_to_front_axle_m + cg_to_rear_axle_m).

cg_to_front_axle_m.sign_convention: distance measured forward from CG along +x (REP-103)
cg_to_front_axle_m.description: Longitudinal distance from centre of gravity to the front axle.

cg_to_rear_axle_m.sign_convention: distance measured aft from CG along -x (REP-103)
cg_to_rear_axle_m.description: Longitudinal distance from centre of gravity to the rear axle.

track_width_m.description: Distance between left/right wheel contact patches. Not modeled by the f1tenth_gym single-track model; null until Phase 1 chassis measurement.

cg_height_m.sign_convention: REP-103: z up positive, measured from ground plane
cg_height_m.description: Height of the centre of gravity above the ground plane.

yaw_inertia_kg_m2.description: Yaw moment of inertia about the vertical axis through the CG.

rear_overhang_m.sign_convention: distance measured aft from the rear axle centre along -x (REP-103)
rear_overhang_m.description: Distance from the rear axle centre back to the rear-most point of the body (the rear bumper line), added 2026-10-06 (schema 0.10.0) for racer_safety/safety_node's rear corridor: a reverse request's in-path distance is measured along the reverse path from this line. Not cg_to_rear_axle_m (that is the CG to the axle, forward of it) and not derivable from length_m, which is a bounding box. The committed value is PROVISIONAL, to be measured on the car.

front_overhang_m.sign_convention: distance measured forward from the front axle centre along +x (REP-103)
front_overhang_m.description: Distance from the front axle centre forward to the front-most point of the body (the front bumper line), added 2026-10-06 (schema 0.11.0). The rear axle to front bumper distance is wheelbase_m + front_overhang_m; the outer front corner of the body sweeps the circle of radius hypot(wheelbase_m + front_overhang_m, R + half width) about the turn centre. racer_safety/safety_node's forward arc corridor takes its outer boundary from that circle, and racer_control's gap follower uses the same front x for its swept-path clamp and forward arc probe. Not derivable from length_m, which is a bounding box. The committed value is PROVISIONAL, to be measured on the car.

linear_cornering_stiffness_front_n_per_r.description: Linear tire model cornering stiffness, front axle. Placeholder pending a full Pacejka fit (see pacejka_front).

linear_cornering_stiffness_rear_n_per_ra.description: Linear tire model cornering stiffness, rear axle. Placeholder pending a full Pacejka fit (see pacejka_rear).

nominal_radius_m.description: Nominal wheel/tire radius. MEASURED and drift-tracked (tires wear); null until measured, see sysid/drift/.

compound_id.description: Tire compound identifier. Placeholder string until Phase 3 tire spec is recorded.

surface_id.description: Running-surface identifier. Placeholder string until the venue surface is surveyed.

kinematic_dynamic_switch_velocity_mps.description: Speed below which the kinematic (rather than dynamic single-track) model is used, per the f1tenth_gym vehicle model.

gear_ratio.description: Motor-to-wheel gear ratio. Null until Phase 1 drivetrain assembly.

pole_pairs.description: Motor pole pair count, used for ERPM <-> wheel speed conversion. Null until the motor is specified/measured.

motor_kv_rad_per_s_per_v.description: Motor velocity constant. Manufacturer datasheets quote Kv in RPM/V; it must be converted to SI at the driver boundary before being written here (CLAUDE.md invariant 4). Null until measured.

current_limit_a.description: Drive current limit, mirrors the VESC layer-2 config. Null until that config exists.

brake_current_limit_a.description: Brake current limit, mirrors the VESC layer-2 config. Null until that config exists.

min_rate_rad_per_s.description: Minimum (fastest rightward) steering rate the servo can achieve.

max_rate_rad_per_s.description: Maximum (fastest leftward) steering rate the servo can achieve.

time_constant_s.description: First-order servo response time constant. Null until measured (Phase 2/3).

pwm_to_angle_table.description: Calibrated servo PWM <-> road-wheel-angle table (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md). Null (not assumed linear) until measured.

pwm_min_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
pwm_min_us.description: Minimum valid steering-servo PWM pulse width, used by firmware/safety_mux (roadmap task 1.3) to reject an out-of-range/glitched Jetson-side steering signal before passing it to the servo. Added for milestone 4 (hardware-arrival prep); null until Phase 1 bench measurement against the actual servo/receiver pair.

pwm_max_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
pwm_max_us.description: Maximum valid steering-servo PWM pulse width, used by firmware/safety_mux (roadmap task 1.3) to reject an out-of-range/glitched Jetson-side steering signal before passing it to the servo. Added for milestone 4 (hardware-arrival prep); null until Phase 1 bench measurement against the actual servo/receiver pair.

pwm_neutral_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
pwm_neutral_us.description: Steering-servo PWM pulse width firmware/safety_mux (roadmap task 1.3) outputs when cutting (kill switch, watchdog timeout, or invalid input) -- centered/straight, not merely 'no signal', so the failsafe does not depend on the servo's own signal-loss behavior. Added for milestone 4; null until Phase 1 bench measurement.

pwm_left_bound.sign_convention: names which of steering.pwm_min_us / steering.pwm_max_us produces a LEFT (positive) road-wheel angle; the other bound is full RIGHT (negative) (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md)
pwm_left_bound.description: Which end of the steering pulse range is full LEFT. MEASURED on the car 2026-09-21 (docs/notes/bench-session-2026-09-20.md): a SHORTER pulse turns the wheels LEFT, so with pwm_min_us < pwm_max_us this is 'pwm_min_us'. Consumed by racer_drivers/pwm_output_node. This used to be an unmeasured node parameter default (steering_left_is_pwm_max, true) rather than a vehicle_params field -- CLAUDE.md invariant 2 treats a sign convention as a physical constant, not a code/launch default, so it moved here once it was actually measured.

command_to_torque_delay_s.description: Measured command-to-torque transport delay. Null until measured.

throttle_time_constant_s.description: First-order throttle response time constant. Null until measured.

throttle_pwm_min_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
throttle_pwm_min_us.description: Minimum valid ESC/throttle PWM pulse width, used by firmware/safety_mux (roadmap task 1.3) to reject an out-of-range/glitched Jetson-side throttle signal before passing it to the ESC. Added for milestone 4 (hardware-arrival prep); null until Phase 1 bench measurement against the actual ESC/receiver pair.

throttle_pwm_max_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
throttle_pwm_max_us.description: Maximum valid ESC/throttle PWM pulse width, used by firmware/safety_mux (roadmap task 1.3) to reject an out-of-range/glitched Jetson-side throttle signal before passing it to the ESC. Added for milestone 4 (hardware-arrival prep); null until Phase 1 bench measurement against the actual ESC/receiver pair.

throttle_pwm_neutral_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
throttle_pwm_neutral_us.description: ESC PWM pulse width firmware/safety_mux (roadmap task 1.3) outputs when cutting (kill switch, watchdog timeout, or invalid input) -- the ESC's documented zero-throttle/brake-neutral value, not merely 'no signal'. Added for milestone 4; null until Phase 1 bench measurement.

throttle_full_scale_mps.sign_convention: positive forward; a commanded -this maps to throttle_pwm_min_us
throttle_full_scale_mps.description: Full-scale speed reference for racer_drivers/pwm_output_node's provisional OPEN-LOOP throttle map: a commanded +this maps to throttle_pwm_max_us and -this to throttle_pwm_min_us. An ACTUATION scale, not a safety limit -- limits.global_speed_cap_mps still clamps the command and is unaffected. Exists because the speed cap (an f1tenth_gym model-validity bound, 20 m/s) made a 1 m/s command only 25 us off neutral, likely inside the VESC PPM deadband (GitHub issue #40). Null until measured; the committed value is PROVISIONAL and unmeasured, replaced by the wheels-off-the-ground throttle sweep in docs/notes/first-boot-runbook.md, and removed entirely when the closed-loop vesc_node replaces the open-loop map.

steering_pwm_period_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM frame period; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
steering_pwm_period_us.description: PWM frame period racer_drivers/pwm_output_node writes to the Jetson's STEERING sysfs PWM channel (period, in ns, is this x 1000). It sets the ACHIEVABLE PULSE GRID and nothing else: the Tegra PWM controller has 8-bit duty resolution (pwm-tegra.c PWM_DUTY_WIDTH 8), so a commanded pulse lands on a multiple of period/256 -- 78.125 us at a 20 ms frame, 15.625 us at 4 ms (GitHub issue #66). It is NOT what the steering servo sees: firmware/safety_mux captures the INPUT pulse width by edge timestamps and REGENERATES its own 50 Hz output to the servo (firmware/safety_mux/pico/pwm_output.c), so this period only exists on the Jetson-to-Pico link. Non-nullable: there is no defensible default for a value that decides actuator resolution, and a consumer must refuse rather than guess (CLAUDE.md invariants 2 and 3). Must be longer than steering.pwm_max_us with room for a low gap between frames; the schema floor of 2500 us is the hard limit and pwm_output_node refuses anything not comfortably above the channel's own pwm_max_us.

throttle_pwm_period_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM frame period; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
throttle_pwm_period_us.description: PWM frame period racer_drivers/pwm_output_node writes to the Jetson's THROTTLE sysfs PWM channel. Same meaning, same grid arithmetic and same non-nullable stance as steering_pwm_period_us; kept per channel because the two channels are different pwmchips on this board (pwmchip0 and pwmchip2) and nothing forces them to share a frame. The VESC never sees this either -- the mux regenerates its own 50 Hz PPM output to the ESC.

steering_pwm_achieved_period_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM frame period; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
steering_pwm_achieved_period_us.description: The frame period the Jetson's STEERING PWM channel ACTUALLY emits when steering_pwm_period_us is requested, MEASURED at the safety mux (GitHub issue #77). The Tegra driver (pwm-tegra.c tegra_pwm_config) converts the requested duty into an 8-bit count against the REQUESTED period, but the frame it emits is 256 x (PWM_SCALE + 1) cycles of whatever rate the PWM clock actually settled at, and no sysfs or debugfs attribute reports that frame (the driver has no get_state; sysfs and /sys/kernel/debug/pwm echo the request). When the two differ every pulse is scaled by achieved/requested. racer_drivers/pwm_output_node pre-scales each duty by requested/achieved so the pulse on the wire is the commanded one. Only valid for the requested period it was measured at: changing steering_pwm_period_us invalidates it. Non-nullable for the same reason as the requested period; set it equal to the requested period only if the bench shows no scaling. pwm_output_node refuses a value more than 5 percent from the requested period (a typo, not a measurement).

throttle_pwm_achieved_period_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM frame period; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
throttle_pwm_achieved_period_us.description: The frame period the Jetson's THROTTLE PWM channel ACTUALLY emits when throttle_pwm_period_us is requested, MEASURED at the safety mux. Same meaning, same compensation and same refusal band as steering_pwm_achieved_period_us (GitHub issue #77); kept per channel because the two channels are different pwmchips with their own clocks.

throttle_deadband_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width offset; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
throttle_deadband_us.description: Offset from throttle_pwm_neutral_us at which racer_drivers/pwm_output_node's open-loop throttle map STARTS for any non-zero speed command: speed 0 maps to exactly throttle_pwm_neutral_us, a speed > 0 maps to neutral + this + a linear share of the rest of the range up to throttle_pwm_max_us at throttle_full_scale_mps (mirrored below neutral for a negative speed). It mirrors the ESC's own PPM deadband (VESC app_ppm_conf.hyst, a fraction of the 500 us half range) so the first non-zero command lands outside it instead of being swallowed. Must be re-set whenever the VESC deadband or centre changes. 0 disables the offset and restores a plain linear map.

imu.description: IMU is designed to mount at the CG (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md); exact offsets are null until Phase 2 ingest-board measurement.

lidar.description: LiDAR mounting pose in base_link (roadmap 2.3). PROVISIONAL values until the mount is measured on the car; racer_bringup/launch/lidar.launch.py publishes the base_link -> laser static transform from these and refuses to start while any of the four pose fields is null.

lidar_spec.description: Datasheet properties of the fitted 2D LiDAR head (roadmap 2.3). These are what racer_tools' lidar_check compares a live /scan against, and what lidar.launch.py hands the driver as its scan_frequency. Datasheet values, not measurements: a measured scan rate goes into a dated docs/notes entry, not here.

model.description: Vendor model of the LiDAR head, for reports and bag provenance.

nominal_scan_rate_hz.description: Typical full-revolution scan rate per the datasheet. Passed to the driver as scan_frequency, which sllidar_ros2 uses to size its angle-compensated beam array.

min_scan_rate_hz.description: Lowest scan rate the datasheet allows. lidar_check fails a scan stream measured below this.

sample_rate_hz.description: Range samples per second per the datasheet.

angular_resolution_rad.description: Angular spacing between samples at the nominal scan rate, per the datasheet.

field_of_view_rad.description: Horizontal field of view per the datasheet (2 pi for a 360 degree head).

range_min_m.description: Minimum measurable range per the datasheet.

range_max_m.description: Maximum measurable range per the datasheet.

global_speed_cap_mps.description: Global forward speed cap enforced by layers 3-4. Sourced here from the f1tenth_gym dynamic-model validity bound (v_max), NOT a validated on-vehicle safety limit; must be re-set conservatively before Phase 1 bench testing.

min_velocity_mps.description: Reverse speed cap enforced by layers 3-4.

ttc_warning_s.description: Time-to-collision warning threshold used by racer_safety/safety_node's layer-3 TTC gate. Null disables the gate. The committed value is PROVISIONAL: a conventional F1TENTH-class starting point, not tuned against this car's measured braking distance.

ttc_brake_s.description: Time-to-collision hard-brake threshold used by racer_safety/safety_node's layer-3 TTC gate. Null disables the gate. The committed value is PROVISIONAL: a conventional F1TENTH-class starting point, not tuned against this car's measured braking distance. Note that safety_node's forward-speed estimate for TTC is its own COMMANDED speed until /odom exists.

min_forward_clearance_m.description: Distance floor for racer_safety/safety_node's layer-3 obstacle gate (added 2026-10-06, schema 0.7.0). If the along-track distance to the nearest valid LiDAR return in the path corridor (obstacle_corridor_margin_m, bounded by ttc_forward_sector_half_angle_rad; schema 0.9.0, before that the whole forward sector and the slant range) is less than this, measured from the LiDAR head, forward throttle is held at zero regardless of the requested speed, latched with the TTC brake and released once that return is farther than this times the gate's release factor (racer_safety/gate_logic.hpp). Catches the crawl-speed case TTC cannot. The committed value is PROVISIONAL, not measured.

ttc_forward_sector_half_angle_rad.sign_convention: symmetric about the vehicle's +x axis (base_link, REP-103); the sector is [-value, +value] in VEHICLE bearing, i.e. after sensors.lidar.mount_yaw_rad is applied to each laser bearing
ttc_forward_sector_half_angle_rad.description: Half angle of the forward sector that bounds racer_safety/safety_node's in-path test for the TTC gate and the distance floor (added 2026-10-06, schema 0.7.0; before that it used the whole 360 degree scan, so self-returns and anything beside or behind the car braked a forward command). Since schema 0.9.0 it is only the OUTER bound: no return outside it is ever considered, whatever obstacle_corridor_margin_m says, and the corridor (obstacle_corridor_margin_m) is the primary filter. The committed value is PROVISIONAL, not tuned.

obstacle_corridor_margin_m.sign_convention: symmetric about the vehicle's +x axis (base_link, REP-103); applied to |y| of each return after sensors.lidar.mount_yaw_rad
obstacle_corridor_margin_m.description: Lateral margin of racer_safety/safety_node's obstacle-gate path corridor (added 2026-10-06, schema 0.9.0). A LiDAR return at vehicle bearing theta and range r (x = r cos theta ahead, y = r sin theta left) counts for the TTC brake and the distance floor only if x > 0, |theta| <= ttc_forward_sector_half_angle_rad (the outer bound) and |y| <= chassis.width_m / 2 + this margin (the primary filter); the distance used is x, not r. Added after the first floor test, where a bag 0.3 m beside the car's path braked it like a bag straight ahead. The committed value is PROVISIONAL, not tuned.

obstacle_steering_hold_after_s.description: Steering hold on racer_safety/safety_node's layer-3 obstacle latch (added 2026-10-06, schema 0.8.0). Once the latch (TTC brake or distance floor) has held the gated output speed at exactly zero for this long, the gate freezes the steering output at the angle it had when the hold started, until the latch releases or a reverse request moves the car. Before that, steering passes as usual (rate-limited), because a car braking at speed must keep steering authority. Zero speed on /drive is a coast and safety_node has no /odom, so this time stands in for 'the car has stopped'. The committed value is PROVISIONAL, not measured.

envelope_fraction_speed.description: Envelope fraction of the speed cap the residual policy may command. Null until tuned (claude-docs/08-learning.md).

envelope_fraction_lateral_accel.description: Envelope fraction of the friction-limited lateral acceleration the residual policy may command. Null until tuned (claude-docs/08-learning.md).

mux_watchdog_timeout_s.description: Layer-1 safety mux (firmware/safety_mux, roadmap task 1.3, claude-docs/05-safety.md): how long the mux MCU waits with no Jetson-side heartbeat before cutting drive/steering PWM and asserting the power cutoff. This is a LAYER-1 constant read only by that firmware's C binding -- it must never be confused with racer_safety's layer-3 /drive_raw watchdog (watchdog_missed_cycles * control_period_s in gate_logic.hpp), which is a separate mechanism on a separate MCU by design. Added for milestone 4 (hardware-arrival prep); null until Phase 1 bench tuning.

mux_kill_switch_threshold_us.units: microseconds (raw PWM pulse width; non-SI driver-boundary value, see CLAUDE.md invariant 4)
mux_kill_switch_threshold_us.description: Layer-1 safety mux (firmware/safety_mux, roadmap task 1.3): PWM pulse width read from the RC receiver's kill-switch channel at or above which the switch reads as ARMED (drive enabled); below this, or outside the receiver's valid PWM range, reads as KILL (fail-safe default). Added for milestone 4; null until the RC receiver/transmitter pair is bench-measured.

schema_version.description: Semver of this params file's schema. Any change bumps this; consumers refuse on a major mismatch (claude-docs/06-vehicle-params.md rule 5).

sysid_session_id.description: The sysid/fitting/ session id that produced these fitted values, or a clearly-provisional placeholder such as 'none-preliminary' when no on-vehicle fit exists yet.

fit_date.description: Date this params file's values were fitted or, for a preliminary file, the date it was assembled from its cited provenance.
